baseline_skill_commit: 3d156fb for pr-review, c1019cd for the other four
skill_changes_summary: Added an ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English output-language section to all five skills. Iterated once within the same session: v2 adds a 'Do not lose information' rule after v1 measurably shed file:line citations.
targets: test-repo/eventbus (copied to a scratchpad dir so no agent can read ground_truth.json)
a private real-world PR — 2 files, +49/-3, infrastructure config (shallow clone, read-only). Run artifacts are gitignored: this repo is public.

arms.base: skills at commit c1019cd, no STE requirement
arms.ste2: working tree, STE section v1 + 'Do not lose information'

harness.runner: run_skill.sh — renders SKILL.md (frontmatter stripped, $ARGUMENTS substituted) and runs it as a standalone prompt in a separate headless process via `cbt -p --output-format json`
harness.why_not_installed_skills: Running the rendered body keeps the current working-tree version and the previous commit's version comparable in the same session, with no writes to ~/.claude/skills.
harness.tools_granted: Read Grep Glob (plus Bash for pr-review). Identical across arms, so the comparison stays differential.

scorers.ste_score.py: sentence length, non-approved words, idioms, passive voice, -ing openers. Prose only: code fences, inline code, headings, field labels, paths, and quoted text are stripped first, because the skills exempt them.
scorers.structure_score.py: template headings and field names present verbatim; enum values valid; severity casing tracked separately
scorers.detail_score.py: information density — quantities, file:line citations, code refs, causal links, all per finding
scorers.gt_score.py: recall against the planted-issue manifest, plus unmatched findings for manual review
scorers.apc_verdict_score.py: verdict accuracy against an answer key built from the planted issues and the false-positive traps

known_limitations: One sample per arm. Differences under roughly 10 percent are not separable from run-to-run variance.

test-repo/eventbus carries `# BUG [CATEGORY]:` annotations in the source, which an auditor can grep. Recall saturates at 1.0 in every arm, so recall cannot detect a small loss of discovery. A blind copy with the annotations removed is the fix.

The eventbus ground truth marks MemoryStorage as clean code. Both arms correctly reported that `_by_topic` grows without a limit, which is a real defect the manifest misses. Precision against this manifest therefore understates both arms.
Noun clusters (STE: at most three nouns together) are not scored. Detection needs part-of-speech tagging.

pr-review ran against one small real PR (2 files, +49/-3), so its numbers are the least generalizable. Its reports quote a private repository, so they are gitignored and scored into benchmark-private.json.
